findings.issue: pkill -f pattern matched the agent's own bash command line, killing the shell (exit 143) — the same mistake made twice, and turn 59's confusion briefly masked a correct fix
findings.suggestion: Record the server PID when launching it, or kill by PID from pgrep output instead of a -f pattern that matches the invoking shell

findings.issue: No TypeScript typecheck was ever run (typechecks: 0) even though the project uses strict mode and the agent knowingly relied on `as`/`as never` casts
findings.suggestion: Run `tsc --noEmit` once before declaring done; it costs one turn and validates the TS config the app ships with

findings.issue: Five turns spent trying unavailable image tools (PIL, pip, ImageMagick) before installing sharp
findings.suggestion: When a capability is missing, jump straight to the ecosystem-native option (npm install sharp) rather than probing for preinstalled tools one by one

findings.issue: Two turns of confused grep-based verification of SSR HTML (React comment nodes splitting text) produced ambiguous output before being correctly interpreted
findings.suggestion: Verify SSR output with a headless browser (which it did later) rather than grep against streamed HTML

summary: A model planning-and-execution trace: requirements, data shapes, edge cases and design tokens were all understood up front, the app was written in one pass that passed all 54 acceptance tests on its first run, and only two real defects (an API rename and a search-param redirect) needed debugging, both diagnosed from evidence. Weaknesses are minor and operational: an image-tooling detour, a twice-repeated pkill self-kill, and no typecheck. Roughly 8 of 96 turns were skippable.
